title: Volunteering at an Animal Shelter
description: Four recordings about helping at an animal shelter: a first meeting, a volunteers' talk, a chat about a dog and a phone message.
instructions: Read the questions for each part first. Then press Play and listen. Choose the best answer (A, B or C) for each question.

parts.title: Part 1 · Joining as a volunteer
parts.intro: You will hear a teenager, Jack, talking to a shelter coordinator, Linh.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Hello, Jack. Thanks for coming in. So, you'd like to volunteer at our animal shelter?

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: Yes, please. I saw your poster at the library. I'm free on Saturdays and on Sunday mornings.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Great. We need the most help on Saturdays. We start at eight, but you can come at nine if that's easier.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: Nine would be better, thanks. I have a swimming lesson at seven, so eight is a bit early for me.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Now, what experience do you have with animals?

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: We have a dog at home, and I used to look after my neighbour's rabbits. I'm not so sure about cats, though. I'm a bit afraid of them.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Don't worry. Most new volunteers begin with the dogs. You'll walk them, fill their water bowls and clean the kennels. Later, if you like, you can help in the cat room.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: That sounds good. Do I need to buy anything special?

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Just old clothes and strong boots. We give you a green shirt with our name on it, and we provide the gloves.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: Perfect. When can I start?

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: This Saturday. Please bring a form signed by your parents, because you're only sixteen.

parts.title: Part 2 · The volunteers' meeting
parts.intro: You will hear the manager, Mr Harris, speaking at a volunteers' meeting.

script.speaker: Mr Harris
script.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to our monthly volunteers' meeting. I'll be quick, because I know you all want to see the new puppies.

script.speaker: Mr Harris
script.text: First, some good news. Last month we found homes for thirty-two animals, which is our best result this year. Well done, everybody.

script.speaker: Mr Harris
script.text: Second, our adoption day is on the fourteenth of June, not the twelfth as it says on the website. We're going to correct that today.

script.speaker: Mr Harris
script.text: On adoption day, we need six people to welcome visitors and four more to show the dogs in the garden. Please put your name on the sheet by the door.

script.speaker: Mr Harris
script.text: Now, a reminder about the rules. Visitors may not feed the animals, even if they say it's only a small biscuit. Some of our dogs have special diets, and the wrong food can make them ill.

script.speaker: Mr Harris
script.text: Also, please don't promise a visitor that a certain dog is a good pet for children. Ask one of the staff. We want every animal to find the right family, not just the first family.

script.speaker: Mr Harris
script.text: Finally, the roof of the cat room has a leak. The builders are coming on Thursday, so for two days the cats will stay in the main hall. It will be noisy, so I'm sorry about that.

script.speaker: Mr Harris
script.text: That's all from me. There are cakes in the kitchen, made by Mrs Parker, so please help yourselves.

parts.title: Part 3 · A difficult dog
parts.intro: You will hear two volunteers, Mai and Tom, talking about a dog called Rocky.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: Hi, Tom. You look tired. Did you have a hard day with Rocky?

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Honestly, yes. He pulled on the lead the whole walk, and then he wouldn't come back inside. I think he's bored.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: He's only two years old and he's full of energy. I usually take him to the field behind the shelter so he can run.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: I didn't know we were allowed. I thought the field was only for staff.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: Actually, volunteers can use it as long as they ask first. Also, try giving him a toy. He loves the red rubber ball.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Good idea. By the way, I heard a family is coming to see him on Saturday.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: Yes, but I'm not sure he's right for them. They have two small children, and Rocky likes to jump up at people.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: That's true. Maybe the manager will suggest an older dog instead.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: I hope so. I'd hate for him to be returned. It happened to a dog last winter, and it was very sad for everyone.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Well, I'll spend extra time training him this week. If he learns to sit calmly, he'll have a better chance.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: That's a lovely plan. I'll help you after lunch on Thursday, if you like.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Thanks, Mai. That would be brilliant.

parts.title: Part 4 · A recorded message
parts.intro: You will hear a recorded message from Hillside Animal Shelter.

script.speaker: Sara
script.text: Thank you for calling Hillside Animal Shelter. Our office is closed at the moment, so please listen carefully to this message.

script.speaker: Sara
script.text: We are open to visitors from ten in the morning until four in the afternoon, Tuesday to Sunday. We are closed on Mondays. On the last Sunday of every month, we close early, at two o'clock, for cleaning.

script.speaker: Sara
script.text: If you'd like to adopt a pet, you must first fill in a form, which you can find on our website. After that, we'll invite you for a short interview and ask you to meet the animal at least twice.

script.speaker: Sara
script.text: The adoption fee is fifty pounds for a cat and seventy pounds for a dog. This covers the vet check, the first injections and a microchip. It does not include food, so you'll need to buy that separately.

script.speaker: Sara
script.text: If you've found a lost or injured animal, please don't wait for us to open. Call the emergency number, which is on our front door and on our website, and a member of staff will help you.

script.speaker: Sara
script.text: If you'd like to give something instead of adopting, we always need blankets, towels and dog toys. We cannot accept old food because of safety rules. Please leave your gifts at the front desk.

script.speaker: Sara
script.text: Thank you for caring about animals, and we hope to see you soon.
